editorial:
You follow Na Bo-ra, a bright teen in 1999 who agrees to watch a boy for her best friend, then finds her own feelings getting complicated. The movie has a warm, nostalgic feel, with school hallways, handwritten notes, and first-love nerves that make the story easy to connect with. Kim Yoo-jung brings a lot of charm to Bo-ra, and the friendship at the center gives the romance real heart. The pacing is gentle but steady, so you get time to care about everyone before the bigger emotions land.

Some moments are predictable, and a few side characters could use more depth, but the emotional payoff is really strong. If you enjoy tender coming-of-age love stories, this is a great pick for a cozy night in. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, adult Bo-ra learns that Woon-ho died in a tragic accident shortly after moving away, and the emails she thought were from him were actually sent by his younger brother. At an exhibition, she sees a video message Woon-ho left for her, realizing he never stopped caring. She finally accepts the loss and lets go of the past.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves tender coming-of-age romance and 90s nostalgia.
